messages:
incident-bot: Pager — HIGH severity: GPU memory surge detected on inference-pool-usw2; repeated container restarts during prefill. Affected service: /v1/generate. Alerts: OOM, CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/incident/1717201234 :rotating_light:
oncall-sre: I'm oncall, taking lead. Starting investigation. Paging eng-runtime & eng-ml.
sre-ian: Confirmed multiple containers restarted on node gpu-usw2-12, prefill allocation spike coincides with long-context requests. I see OOM in logs: `2024-10-02T23:07:12Z ERROR cuda: out of memory allocating 12.3GiB`
eng-runtime-amy: joining. Is this the long-window prefill path? Any recent deploys?
sre-ian: No deploys in last 6h. CPU backpressure low. Prefill request histogram shows a spike of seq_len > 100k tokens from a single customer route.
eng-ml-chen: That matches model kv-cache blowout. We can temporarily enforce prefill truncation (max_prefill_tokens=8192) as mitigation. Can runtime push a per-route throttle?
oncall-sre: Eng-runtime, can you push a hot-config to enforce truncation + reject >8192 with 429? Also enable fallback to smaller model variant.
eng-runtime-amy: Pushing hotfix: add per-route prefill cap 8192, route throttle 10rps, attach fallback to small-gpt-quant. Will roll canary 10% then 100%.
incident-bot: Deploybot: rollout started for config hotfix-1717201234 -> canary 10%
support-maya: Support note: Beginning to triage customer error reports. Initial customers impacted: AcmeApp (50 errs/min), BetaAI (sporadic).
cs-luke: Reached out to AcmeApp with initial notice: 'We are investigating GPU memory errors affecting long-context requests; temporary mitigations in progress.'
eng-runtime-amy: Canary passed at 10%; promoting to 100%. Rolling now.
incident-bot: Deploybot: rollout complete -> 100%
sre-ian: After config roll, OOMs dropped to zero on node gpu-usw2-12. Error rate on /v1/generate back to baseline. Throttle metrics show reduced tail latency.
eng-ml-chen: Plan for next steps: 1) add per-tenant hard caps for prefill by default, 2) model-side kv pruning for extreme sequence, 3) add synthetic load tests for seq_len 200k.
oncall-sre: Great. Please also schedule a postmortem and customer follow-up. I'll close pager when we have stable metrics for 15m.
support-maya: CS will follow up with detailed impact and timeline.
